content: Sulfacetamide (topical) is an FDA-approved antibacterial and anti-acne medication used for the treatment of acne vulgaris. Common side effects include irritation at the application site. For adult patients, sulfacetamide sodium lotion is applied topically as a thin film to the affected areas twice daily. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of sulfacetamide in adults, though it has been mentioned in the context of bacterial keratitis. In pediatric patients, there is limited information regarding both FDA-labeled and off-label uses of sulfacetamide sodium lotion. Its safety and effectiveness in children under the age of 12 have not been established. Sulfacetamide sodium lotion is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to sulfonamides or any other component of the preparation. Severe reactions to sulfonamides, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, fulminant hepatic necrosis, agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia, and other blood dyscrasias, have been reported, though they are rare. Hypersensitivity reactions may occur even in individuals without a prior history of sulfonamide sensitivity. At the first sign of hypersensitivity, such as a skin rash or other reaction, the medication should be discontinued. The lotion contains sodium metabisulfite, which may cause allergic-type reactions, including anaphylaxis and life-threatening or less severe asthmatic episodes in susceptible individuals. Sulfite sensitivity is more common in asthmatic individuals than in non-asthmatics. Sulfacetamide sodium lotion is for external use only and should be kept away from the eyes. If irritation develops, the product should be discontinued, and appropriate therapy should be initiated. Patients should be monitored for local irritation or sensitization during long-term therapy. Cross-sensitivity between different sulfonamides may occur. The lotion can cause redness and scaling of the skin, particularly in areas of denuded or abraded skin. It should be kept out of the reach of children. In clinical trials for acne vulgaris, adverse reactions associated with sulfacetamide sodium lotion were infrequent and primarily limited to local events. The total incidence of adverse reactions was less than 2%. Reported reactions included erythema, itching, and edema. Local irritation, stinging, and burning have also been reported, though these effects are often transient. Occasionally, the medication must be discontinued due to irritation. There is limited information regarding postmarketing experience, drug interactions, and the use of sulfacetamide sodium lotion in specific populations, including pregnant women, nursing mothers, geriatric patients, and immunocompromised individuals. Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted, and it is not known whether the lotion can cause fetal harm when administered to pregnant women. Sulfacetamide sodium lotion should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. Kernicterus has been reported in newborns following the treatment of pregnant women at term with orally administered sulfonamides. It is also unknown whether sulfacetamide sodium lotion is excreted in human milk following topical use, though systemic sulfonamides are known to be excreted in small amounts in breast milk. The pharmacological mechanism of action of sulfacetamide is based on the Woods-Fildes theory, where sulfonamides act as competitive inhibitors of para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) utilization, an essential component for bacterial growth. The lotion contains 10% sodium sulfacetamide in a vehicle consisting of purified water, propylene glycol, lauramide DEA, polyethylene glycol 400 monolaurate, hydroxyethyl cellulose, sodium chloride, sodium metabisulfite, methylparaben, xanthan gum, EDTA, and simethicone. In vitro studies with human cadaver skin indicate approximately 4% percutaneous absorption. When taken orally, sodium sulfacetamide is readily absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract and excreted in the urine largely unchanged, with a biological half-life of 7 to 13 hours. Sulfacetamide sodium lotion is supplied in 4 fl oz (118 mL) bottles and should be stored at controlled room temperature (20 to 25°C or 68 to 77°F). The bottle should be shaken well before use and kept tightly closed.
